newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas futures sink late on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas futures sink late on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures, pressured by revised forecasts calling for milder weather later this week, fell sharply late Thursday, but trade remained sluggish due to the holiday-shortened week.
At 1340 EST, spot-February tumbled 39.5 cents to $3.31 per million British thermal units, while March was 30.8 cents lower at $2.94. Other months were down by eight to 15 cents.

"Things look pretty soft and could continue that way with the (mild) weather," said one Houston-based trader, referring to 6-10 day forecasts calling for above-normal temperatures for most of the nation.
Despite the midweek Arctic blast hitting northern tier states, traders said more moderate weather on the horizon turned sentiment more bearish today.

In addition, they said some technical factors also turned "Technically, we've got a double top and an island reversal on the perpetual chart, and we filled the $3.47-3.475 gap in February. It's starting to look ugly," an East Coast trader said.
Next support in February was seen in $3.20 area, with psychological buying likely at $3.00. Resistance was pegged at today's gap at $3.595-3.61 and then at the contract high of $4.02.
A Reuter poll of industry players showed most expected later today a weekly AGA stock draw of between 110 and 120 bcf versus last year's draw of 133.
In the cash, December Hub skidded more than 20 cents to the low-to-mid $3.50s, with January talked in the low-$3.70s. December Midcontinent gas slipped a dime to the $3.55-3.60 area.
